content: Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Liquid forms of this medication should not be frozen. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the product is expired or no longer needed, dispose of it properly. This information was last updated in May 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common Brand Names: Benadryl, Genahist, Naramine, Sominex, Unisom. Uses: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine used to alleviate symptoms of allergies, hay fever, and the common cold. These symptoms include rash, itching, watery eyes, itchy eyes/nose/throat, cough, runny nose, and sneezing. It is also used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness. This medication works by blocking histamine, a natural substance produced by the body during an allergic reaction. Cough and cold products have not been proven safe or effective in children under 6 years of age. Do not use this product to treat cold symptoms in children younger than 6 years unless directed by a doctor. Certain products, such as long-acting tablets or capsules, are not recommended for children under 12 years. These products do not cure or shorten the duration of the common cold and may cause serious side effects. To minimize the risk of serious side effects, follow all dosage instructions carefully. Do not use this product to make a child sleepy. Avoid giving other cough-and-cold medications that may contain the same or similar ingredients. How to Use: Follow all instructions on the product packaging. If prescribed by your doctor, take the medication as directed. Take the tablet, capsule, or liquid form by mouth with or without food. Rapidly dissolving tablets or strips should be allowed to dissolve on the tongue before swallowing, with or without water. Dosage is based on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. There are many brands and forms of diphenhydramine available, so read the dosing instructions carefully for each product, as the amount of diphenhydramine may vary. To prevent motion sickness, take your dose 30 minutes before starting activities such as travel. To aid sleep, take your dose approximately 30 minutes before bedtime. Side Effects: Common side effects may include drowsiness, dizziness, constipation, stomach upset, blurred vision, or dry mouth/nose/throat. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking diphenhydramine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to dimenhydrinate, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. Liquid products, chewable tablets, or dissolving tablets/strips may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Liquid products may also contain alcohol. Use caution if you have diabetes, liver disease, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Older adults may also be more sensitive, particularly to drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Diphenhydramine passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications (such as allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (such as allergy skin tests), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Symptoms of overdose may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or widened pupils. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not freeze liquid forms of this medication. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
